title: Understanding SVD
text: In Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), a matrix X is decomposed into three matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. The matrix S contains the singular values, which are always non-negative and arranged in descending order. These values give us insight into the variance captured by each principal component.

title: Properties of V Matrix
text: The columns of the V matrix in SVD are orthonormal vectors. This means each column has a norm of $$1$$, and the dot product between any two different columns is $$0$$.
